subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Transistor History: From Bell Labs to Billions
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Transistor History: From Bell Labs to Billions.

hook.text: In 1947, three Bell Labs scientists pressed a gold contact onto germanium. The transistor was born.

buildup.text: Bardeen, Brattain, and Shockley won the 1956 Nobel Prize for their invention.

discovery.text: The point-contact transistor was fragile. The junction transistor that followed was reliable.

twist.text: Shockley left Bell Labs and founded a company in Silicon Valley — naming the region forever.

climax.text: From one hand-assembled transistor to chips with 100 billion — in just 75 years.

punchline.text: One gold contact on germanium launched the entire digital age.
